thread:
maria chen: CI canary failed: audit-event-validator reported a missing required field 'actor_id' on a customer-visible emit sample. Minimal log below.

maria chen: ```
FAIL: samples/emit/login-0007.json
AssertionError: required field 'actor_id' not found
payload: {"event_type":"login","actor":{"display":"alice@example.com"},"ts":1680000000}
```

alex r: that aligns with the RBAC prune we landed last week. we switched internal traces to embed actor.display and removed actor_id from some paths. i thought we left an adapter for audit events though.

jia wang: is this failing against main or the feature branch? our CI pulls the canonical corpus from s3://redwood-audit-contracts/current — if the corpus wasn't updated after the RBAC change we'll see these false negatives.

deploy-bot: Job audit-schema-checker #789 failed: 1 failing sample, 9 passed. Logs: https://ci.redwood.example/builds/789 :warning:

leo p: easiest unblock: make the validator accept both shapes (compat shim) so the canary passes. followup: refresh canonical samples and schedule a deprecation window.

maria chen: agreed — customer-facing events are a public contract. short-term shim + corpus migration + changelog + CI gate.

alex r: proposed tasks:
1) validator: compatibility layer for actor_id vs actor.display
2) corpus: migration script to produce transitional samples (both fields) and push to s3/current
3) CI: add required audit-schema-checker status on PRs touching emitters
4) docs: release notes + example schemas + deprecation timeline
who takes what?

jia wang: i'll take corpus migration (2). will run s3 sync + normalization and add a checksum file. ETA: today EOD. ping me sample ids to prioritize.

leo p: i'll open the validator patch (1). plan: tiny compatibility check, unit tests for both shapes, and an inline TODO to remove after X releases. example tests: ```python
def test_accepts_actor_display():
    e = {"event_type":"login", "actor":{"display":"alice@example.com"}, "ts":1680000000}
    assert validate_event(e)

def test_accepts_actor_id():
    e = {"event_type":"login", "actor_id":"user_123", "ts":1680000000}
    assert validate_event(e)
```

maria chen: also add a test for KMS-encrypted payloads — previously anonymization removed KMS metadata and validator couldn't map actor. test that encrypted_payload preserves actor mapping metadata.

alex r: i'll add the CI gate (3). we already run the linter; i'll add audit-schema-checker as a required status check on the repo and wire deploy-bot to display results.

maria chen: opened incident note: https://wiki.redwood.example/security/audit-contract-regression — linking this thread. once the validator PR lands and jia promotes the corpus we'll re-run the canary and promote if green.

leo p: PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/audit-validator/pull/352 — includes shim + tests. tagging @maria @alex for quick review.

jia wang: starting corpus migration. will normalize actor shapes to a transitional schema that includes both actor_id and actor.display where resolvable. will include a checksum and a small migration log.

maria chen: thanks. once corpus is uploaded i'll trigger the canary job. if it passes we merge and then schedule a deprecation RFC for removing actor_id in 3 releases. :eyes:
